transcript:
Meeting: Commercial acceptance, timing and tech gating
Date: 2025-12-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Tom Reyes (Procurement, Helios), Priya Nair (Head of Platform), Lucas Grant (Security), Ellen Moore (Legal)

Summary: Quick alignment on MSA/DPA redline path, SLA thresholds for Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS/HSM keying options and egress/cost gating. Agreed next steps around redlines, a short private-deploy bench and procurement timing.

Topics: MSA exceptions, DPA subprocessors, SLA latency targets, dedicated capacity pricing, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs/retention, procurement gating timeline.

-- Transcript --
00:00 Jordan: All right good morning, afternoon everyone. Thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account. Maya, do you want to intro briefly?
00:08 Maya: Yeah hey, Maya Lin, Solutions Engineer. We'll try to keep this practical — focus on the contract asks and what we can deliver from a tech gating perspective.
00:16 Tom: Hey team, Tom here on procurement. We're mostly trying to understand timing and any nonstandard clauses that will block signoff.
00:23 Priya: Priya — Platform. We're primarily worried about network topology, keying, and the SLA tiers — do we need dedicated infra for our latency targets.
00:31 Lucas: Lucas from InfoSec, quick note on auditability and retention. We have a baseline SOC2 checklist and specific audit-log retention requirements.
00:38 Ellen: Ellen, Legal — I'll be reviewing the MSA/DPA redlines. I'd like a clear mapping of which DPA subprocessors are used and data flow diagrams if we can.
00:46 Jordan: Perfect. High level: Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private (VPC or on-prem) deployments. For Helios we recommended dedicated or private based on your latency and data residency asks. Today we want to surface any hard blockers.
00:59 Tom: Procurement timeline — we need procurement committee signoff by Jan 8 to align with next quarter budgets. So if legal and security can sign off earlier that's ideal.
01:07 Jordan: Understood. Maya, on the tech side can you speak to the dedicated SLA and what we can commit?
01:14 Maya: Sure. For Dedicated we have an SLA baseline of 99.9% instance availability and per-token p95 latency windows for common model families. For private deployments we can provide an SLA on the control plane and a runbook for escalation — but exact numbers depend on the deployment topology and whether you want vendor-managed nodes or self-hosted.
01:33 Priya: Is that 99.9% with burst capacity? Because our trading teams need consistent p95 under load spikes.
01:41 Maya: We offer burst pools — you can commit to a baseline throughput and then have auto-burst. That changes pricing; Jordan will walk through committed capacity slides after. The important bit is we can route critical routes to reserved pools to keep jitter low.
01:56 Jordan: On pricing, there are three levers: committed capacity (monthly), burst, and quantization/latency profile. We'll send a model-specific worksheet.
02:06 Ellen: On the MSA, Helios is seeing three asks: tighter indemnity language, vendor audit rights, and specific data deletion clauses. Is Redwood flexible on data deletion timelines?
02:17 Jordan: Yes, we can commit to data deletion from user-accessible storage per the DPA timelines, and for hosted API we offer configurable retention. For private deployments customers control retention. For deletion from backups we can include a reasonable timeline; Maya, what's typical?
02:28 Maya: Generally our hosted retention default is 30 days but we can offer 0-day retention for enterprise plans, and for Dedicated we can scope it to not persist user payloads. For backups it's usually a 90 day window but we can put accelerated purge language in the DPA with escrow exceptions.
02:41 Lucas: We need audit logs for all access to keys and admin operations, and retention for logs of 3 years for certain transactions — that may be longer than Redwood's defaults.
02:52 Maya: We can forward the audit log schema. There's an enterprise plan that ships with extended retention and offsite log export. For timelines on retention we'll need to map which logs are critical — admin, key access, model version rollouts, etc.
03:07 Tom: From procurement side, are there any nonstandard financial clauses — e.g., escrow, termination for convenience that we should flag?
03:14 Jordan: We typically offer standard SaaS terms with 60-day termination windows for annual contracts. For enterprise we can bake in extended notice or escrow for model artifacts on request.
03:25 Priya: KMS — Helios uses an HSM-backed KMS for keys. We need to understand whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys in a cloud HSM or on-prem HSM.
03:36 Maya: We support KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed keying with HSM via application-level wrapping. For private deployments where you control the nodes, the keys never leave your network. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer CMKs where possible, but some low-level signing keys we manage for runtime.
03:55 Lucas: That "some we manage" phrasing is a bit vague. We need specifics: which keys are tenant-controlled, which are Redwood-managed, and where are they stored. Also proof of HSM attestation would be required.
04:06 Maya: Makes sense. We'll produce a diagram and a matrix of key ownership and attestation options.
04:13 Ellen: On subprocessors in the DPA, list of infra providers plus analytics vendors — is Redwood able to provide a subprocessors registry?
04:20 Jordan: Yes we maintain a registry and can provide the current list and a commit to notify for changes.
04:25 Tom: Great. On timing, if you deliver the redline summary and the DPA matrix by the 22nd, procurement can slot this for the Dec 30 review and then final legal by Jan 6.
04:36 Jordan: We can do that. Action item for us to deliver a redline summary and the DPA/subprocessor matrix by Monday (12/22).
04:42 Maya: Quick question — about the tech validation bench. Priya, are you expecting a full replay of your workload or a short synthetic?
04:48 Priya: Short synthetic is fine to validate p95 and KV cache behavior, but we also want an option for a longer run if results look promising. We need to surface costs for the bench too.
04:57 Jordan: We'll propose a 4-hour bench on a mirror dataset and show p50/p95/p99, cost estimate and a quick runbook.
05:05 Lucas: Regarding logs and retention — also need to confirm export format for SIEM ingestion. CSV/JSON syslog?
05:12 Maya: JSON via syslog or S3 export are supported. We'll include sample log snippets.
05:19 Ellen: There was a point about indemnity — we may need to limit Redwood's liability exposure to direct damages with a cap tied to fees. Is that standard for Redwood?
05:28 Jordan: Our standard is mutual limitation of liability with a cap of 12 months' fees for commercial customers, but we're flexible to discuss depending on company policy.
05:37 Tom: That is likely acceptable. We'll table exact numbers until we see the redline.
05:42 Priya: One more technical gating item: networking egress. Our compliance says traffic must remain in EU region for some workloads. Can you pin compute region and control egress?
05:52 Maya: Yes we can pin routes by region and we can provide VPC peering for private deployments. For hosted we have region options and will not route across regions unless configured.
06:02 Jordan: To avoid surprises, we'll add a network diagram and egress controls to the materials.
06:07 Lucas: Any customer-supplied software on Redwood nodes? We have concerns about third-party agents.
06:12 Maya: For private deployments you control node images. For dedicated we run a managed runtime but limit third-party agents; we can provide a list of runtime sidecars.
06:22 Ellen: On the DPA we may ask for a contractual right to conduct audits or request reports — SOC2 plus an annual pen test report.
06:31 Jordan: SOC2 is standard and we'll provide SOC2 Type II reports. For pen tests we can provide summaries or agree to a process for co-ordinated testing.
06:40 Priya: How long to turn up a dedicated pool once contracted? Our internal ops needs it within two weeks ideally.
06:46 Jordan: For Reserved Dedicated capacity we can usually provision in 7-10 business days after countersign and initial payment, depending on capacity availability. For private deployments on-prem timeline is customer dependent.
06:58 Tom: That's helpful. Procurement will need payment milestones and a cancellation clause.
07:04 Jordan: We'll include payment milestones in the commercial paper.
07:07 Maya: Small note on model variants: we can route to quantized variants to reduce cost for lower-latency paths — that might be a lever for you to keep costs down while meeting latency.
07:18 Priya: Worth exploring. We'll want to see quality delta tests.
07:22 Jordan: We'll include sample evals for the model families we discussed.
07:26 Ellen: Last item from legal: export controls and data residency. We will want explicit language that restricts data transfer for EU-resident data.
07:35 Jordan: We can include territory carve-outs and addendum language.
07:38 Tom: Recap — procurement needs: redline summary + DPA matrix by 12/22, pricing worksheet and committed capacity options by 12/20, short tech bench week of 1/5 if possible.
07:51 Jordan: Correct. We'll deliver those docs and loop back.
07:55 Lucas: Action on Redwood: send audit log schema, keying matrix, sample SOC2 report.
08:02 Maya: We'll also send a KMS/HSM integration runbook and sample logs.
08:07 Priya: I'll assemble a short stakeholder map and pass the gating criteria to Tom's procurement tracker.
08:13 Ellen: Legal will prepare a list of non-starter redlines but we'll start with the summary.
08:18 Jordan: Anything else?
08:20 Tom: No, that's it from procurement. Appreciate the quick alignment.
08:24 Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and set up the bench schedule.

End of call.

References shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/security/dpa_matrix (redwood DPA matrix - REDACTED), pricing worksheet link, SOC2 report (redwood-soc2-2025.pdf).

Notes about transcript quality: speaker overlaps minor, occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "MS A" for MSA, "K V cache" instead of KV cache).
